close_reason: Answered by the owner (2026-09-25): compiling and running the def/defp macro root on every compile is intended -- the cost of def as a real macro, for metaprogramming and Elixir-style source. The s1 ledger (scratchpad wave2/r_s1_ledger/ledger.md) audited the def/1 chain's 13 jobs: every one is read by a named consumer; the only fold found (ExpandFunctionSource into DefineFunction) applies to every function and is fz-afu.7.
description:
Every compile runs two nested backend compiles for the `def/1` and `defp/1`
macros. Roots 1 and 2 (backend products for Kernel def/1 and defp/1) are
requested mid-compile while library source is indexed; on
`def main(), do: Enum.take([1, 2, 3], 2)` they span from ~5ms to ~280ms of a
~300ms front end, and each census test pays it once per compile.

Question for the owner before any work: is expanding library `def`/`defp`
through a compiled macro root on every compile intended? If the expansion is
the same on every compile, its product is a fixed fact of the library source.
A reader measures what the two roots cost (jobs and time) and what they
produce, on the reduced case.
title: Every compile runs nested backend compiles for def/1 and defp/1
